notes:
Gaps / low-confidence items, and methodology notes:
(1) West Bengal, Assam and Sikkim underwent (or in Sikkim's case, did not undergo) their scheduled 2025-2026 elections; all office-holder facts below were cross-checked against at least one primary Wikipedia infobox/table fetched live via the Wikipedia parse API on 2026-09-25, not from training-data memory. Two WebFetch summarisation passes were caught inventing plausible-looking but unverifiable detail (a full 'Adhikari ministry' roster, and a 'Manoj Kumar Agarwal' Chief Secretary claim) -- both were independently re-verified against the raw HTML tables (via curl + bs4) before being trusted; the Manoj Kumar Agarwal / Ravi Kota / Ravindra Telang Chief-Secretary trio and the DGP trio were each cross-confirmed against two independent Wikipedia pages (the state government/police infobox AND the 'Chief secretary (India)' / 'Director general of police' national roster tables).
(2) West Bengal: BJP's landslide 2026 win (208/294 initial tally; assembly infobox shows 207 after adjustments) makes Suvendu Adhikari the first BJP Chief Minister of West Bengal, ending Mamata Banerjee's tenure (she lost her own Bhabanipur seat to Adhikari). No Deputy CM was appointed. The Assembly's infobox does not yet list a Deputy Speaker -- recorded vacant/low-confidence, likely just not yet elected at time of the source snapshot. The West Bengal State Election Commissioner and Public Service Commission Chair could not be confirmed with high confidence: the WBSEC Wikipedia infobox names a 'Chief Electoral Officer' (Neelam Meena) under a parent body of 'Election Commission of India', which looks like a conflation of the (ECI-linked) CEO office with the constitutionally distinct Article-243K State Election Commission -- flagged low confidence rather than guessed at. WB Public Service Commission Chairperson is listed as Vacant on Wikipedia (possibly stale). WB State Human Rights Commission chairperson unconfirmed (vacant/low confidence). Kolkata Municipal Corporation's ruling party is shown as 'TBD' in the source table (a KMC election was pending/due in 2026) so no mayor is recorded.
(3) Assam: the NDA (BJP+AGP+BPF) retained power in the April 2026 election (102/126 seats); Himanta Biswa Sarma continues as CM under the 'Second Sarma ministry' (formed 12 May 2026). The 16-member council-of-ministers table published on Wikipedia does not distinguish Cabinet Minister vs Minister-of-State rank (unlike West Bengal's table), so all 16 non-CM ministers are recorded at rank cabinet_minister with a note flagging this assumption; individual constituencies were not published in that table (only home-division groupings) so are omitted rather than guessed. Assam's Lokayukta entry actually names an 'Upa-Lokayukta' (Deputy) -- Justice Hitesh Kumar Sarma -- the full Lokayukta's current occupant was not independently confirmed, so this is flagged medium confidence. Assam State Election Commissioner, Public Service Commission Chairman and Human Rights Commission Chairperson could not be confirmed within the tools available (no populated Wikipedia infobox; apsc.nic.in could not be fetched due to a TLS certificate error) -- all three recorded vacant/low confidence rather than invented.
(4) Sikkim: no assembly election occurred in 2025-2026 (last election 2024, next due 2029); Prem Singh Tamang (SKM) continues as CM, and SKM holds all 32 assembly seats, so there is no Leader of Opposition. The Deputy Chief Minister post is recorded Vacant per the Government of Sikkim infobox. Sikkim has no State Human Rights Commission (no such body found; omitted rather than invented -- distinct from an unconfirmed-holder case). Sikkim's State Election Commission and Lokayukta entities repeat the same 'parent department: Election Commission of India' labelling oddity noted for West Bengal above; the named office-holders (K. C. Lepcha; Justice A. P. Subba) are recorded at medium/high confidence since they come from otherwise well-formed infoboxes, but the parent-body labelling itself is not repeated as fact.
(5) Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha seat counts (WB 42/16, Assam 14/7, Sikkim 1/1) reflect the current (pre-2026-census) delimitation, which has not changed since the last delimitation freeze; Rajya Sabha counts were cross-checked against the Rajya Sabha state-wise allocation table. District counts, area and 2011 census population are from each state's Wikipedia infobox.
(6) Municipal corporations: full lists for all three states (7 in West Bengal, 3 in Assam, 1 in Sikkim) are from Wikipedia's 'List of municipal corporations in India' state-by-state tables; mayors were not separately verified per the task's 'if easily verifiable' allowance and are omitted (only ruling party is recorded where the source table gave one).
(7) High Courts serving each state (Calcutta HC for WB, Gauhati HC for Assam, Sikkim HC for Sikkim) are judiciary-segment-owned and referenced only by their canonical in-hc-* ids, not redefined here.
(8) Party abbreviation DTC (West Bengal's post-defeat AITC breakaway, led into opposition by Ritabrata Banerjee) = Democratic Trinamool Congress; MAITC in both West Bengal and Assam assembly tallies appears to denote a Mamata-aligned AITC remnant/rebrand, not independently resolved beyond the Wikipedia infobox label.
(9) The WebSearch tool's shared session budget (200 calls) was already exhausted by other parallel segment agents before this segment began; all research after that point used WebFetch, curl + the Wikipedia parse API, and python/bs4 table parsing instead, which is why methodology note (1) above exists.
